answer.text: The financial returns to the impact investor, measured in IRR and MOIC
The effect on people and communities that happens as a result of an action or inaction, an activity, project, programme or policy
Only the quantitative output count of a programme over 12 months
The CSR spend divided by beneficiary count

explanation.text: The Logic: Per workbook p.19, 'social impact' is the effect on people and communities that happens as a result of an action or inaction, an activity, project, programme or policy. It is broader than mere output counts or financial ratios. The Trap: Option A mixes impact with financial returns. Option C narrows the definition to quantitative output counts. Option D reduces impact to a per-beneficiary spend ratio. Note: Distinguishing social impact from output and outcome (see p.22) is foundational to assessing claims accurately.
